This is a simple "minimax regret" algorithm, the standard approach for negotiating in uncertain environments with competitive agents. The main idea is that the agent should avoid selecting moves that it would regret in any of the possible states of the world. In the current turn, this can be calculated by considering all the possible moves of the opponent, what states of the world would result, and what the agent's regret would be in each of those states. The agent selects the move with the lowest minimax regret. In the first two turns of the negotiation this is a simple calculation because the agent knows the opponent will accept the offer, so the agent's regret in all states is zero. In the third turn, the agent has no idea how the opponent will respond, so the regret calculation must consider all possible responses. The regret calculation must also take into account the agent's objective, which is to maximize the price. Thus, for example, the agent will reject an offer of 40 for a bike that it values at 60, because the agent will regret receiving 40 over the 60 it wants. In the context of a bargaining game, a Nash equilibrium is a set of reservation prices where no party has an incentive to deviate from its chosen price.
